      <h1 class="talk-title">From Idea to Production: Building an Agentic Forecasting Ecosystem in the Open</h1>
    </header>

    <!-- Body Section -->
    <div class="talk-body">
      
      <!-- Main Description -->
      <section class="talk-description">
        Over the past two decades, open-source forecasting software has transformed how we build forecasting workflows. Rather than focusing solely on algorithms, practitioners and researchers have built an ecosystem of open-source forecasting tools, each exposing different interfaces and often even different programming languages. Agentic forecasting builds on this foundation by introducing large language models as orchestration layers that can reason about forecasting tasks while leveraging the rich ecosystem of existing methods.

In this talk, we will share the lessons we learned while building TimeCopilot, an open-source agentic forecasting framework developed in the open. We'll explore the engineering decisions behind bringing together foundation models and classical forecasting methods under a common interface, the challenges of making LLM-driven workflows reliable, and the trade-offs involved in designing software that remains transparent and reproducible as the ecosystem evolves.

Beyond the architecture itself, we'll discuss what it means to build an AI ecosystem in the open. How do you design APIs for a landscape where models change every few months? How do you balance rapid experimentation with long-term maintainability? And how do you create infrastructure that supports both research prototypes and production deployments? We'll close by reflecting on where agentic forecasting is headed and why the next advances may come as much from software engineering and open collaboration as from the models themselves.
      </section>
